turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr. Hale, come on through. Parking lot was a mess, your son said he circled twice. He answered the intake while you parked. He told me the room spins every time you stand up, you've been nauseated all day, and you've been unsteady and nearly fell in the kitchen yesterday.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. The traffic on Maple was dreadful, yes. I must correct my son on the medical points, if I may. I have not been unsteady, and I did not nearly fall. The spinning is not brought on by standing.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Okay. Both versions stay in the note. Vitals are in. Blood pressure is 138 over 84, heart rate seventy six, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I appreciate that. I took my amlodipine before I left the house.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor Ellison is finishing a call. Have a seat, she'll be right in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr. Hale. Sorry, I was uh stuck on the phone. I saw the intake. What brought you in today, in your own words?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, doctor. Since last week I have had a spinning sensation. It lasts, well, actually, only a few seconds, not longer. It comes when I turn over in bed, or when I look up.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Seconds, not minutes. Umm, I'm already wondering about the little crystals in the inner ear, but let me not jump. How often in a day?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Four or five times, I would estimate. If I hold still, it stops.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the nausea. Is it all day, the way your son put it, or only with the spin? Have you vomited?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Only with the spinning, doctor. It is not all day. I have not vomited.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good, that's clearer. Any hearing loss, either ear?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My hearing has not changed.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ear pain?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No ear pain.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ringing, fullness, drainage?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): None of those. No ringing, no fullness, and no drainage.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Headache with the spells? Double vision, trouble speaking, weakness?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of those.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or pounding in the chest?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Quick sweep of the lungs. Any trouble breathing, cough, wheeze?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): My breathing is perfectly fine.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): You've been on amlodipine how long, and at what dose?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Eight years, for the blood pressure. Five milligrams every morning, by mouth.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else you actually take?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Lipitor, forty milligrams at bedtime, for my cholesterol. Last week an urgent care physician prescribed meclazine, 25 milligrams twice a day, for the spinning. I took it for two days and then I stopped, because it made me far too sleepy. He also wrote for ondansetran, which I never took.

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Meclizine, yes, people spell it meclazine. So the meclizine is stopped. The ondansetron was never started, and I won't list a medicine you never took. Any allergies to medicines or foods?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke? And who's at home?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I live with my son. He is attentive, even when he speaks for me.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Ears first. Both canals are clear and the drums look normal, no redness. Squeeze my fingers. Good, I don't see any focal weakness in the arms.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): That is reassuring. Thank you.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Now the positional test, the Dix-Hallpike. I'll turn your head toward the right and lay you back. It may spin for a moment, and that's, err, what I'm looking for. Ready?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Please go ahead.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): There it is. A burst of torsional nystagmus, right side, about eight or ten seconds, then it fades. I'll check the left. No, I don't see nystagmus on the left.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): It did spin, just as it does at home. It has passed now.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): So, thinking it through. Spins of a few seconds, rolling over or looking up, nausea without hearing loss, and that right-sided torsional nystagmus that fatigues. My working impression is benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, loose crystals in the right posterior canal. Provisional, not something a scan has proved.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. Is there an exercise I should learn?

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, the Epley for the right ear. Sit up, turn your head about forty five degrees, lie back, then roll onto the side, then sit up again. We'll walk through one cycle now, slow. Don't snap the neck.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Like this? Forgive me if the angle is poor.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's the one. Hold each spot about thirty seconds, or until the spinning quits. At home, three cycles in the morning and three in the evening, until I see you. If a cycle makes you very sick, stop and sit, and don't drive while you're spinning.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Three cycles, morning and evening. I shall follow that exactly.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Plan next, and I'm separating what is booked from what is only a maybe. I was going to say Wednesday for bloods, no, Thursday morning. At sixty eight, on the Lipitor, I still want a fasting metabolic panel and a TSH, so a thyroid or a salt problem isn't hiding. The nurse draws those Thursday morning, water only after midnight, and take the amlodipine with a small sip and nothing else.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning. I can arrange that.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll also book an audiogram, a hearing test, for Tuesday at ten. Not because I think the hearing is down, I want a baseline on the chart. That one is definite. The desk can lock it in.
[SEG0047] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can book both from here. Blood draw Thursday at 8 in the morning, and audiology Tuesday at 10. They're on the schedule.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good, those two happen. If the Thursday labs come back borderline, then we do a third test, a hemoglobin A1c, and I'm not ordering that today. If the spinning has not settled, we would get an MRI of the brain. If it has settled, no scan.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): When would you like me to return?
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): In two weeks, either way. I'll see you in two weeks, and the scan only comes up if you are still spinning.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I am grateful for the explanation, and I will do the exercises as you taught them.

spec.situation: Spinning for a few seconds when turning in bed or looking up, since last week; nausea; no hearing loss, no ear pain; doctor does a positional test and teaches the exercise.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Patient denied breathing trouble, but did not specifically deny cough or wheeze.
bad.text: respiratory (status=negative, details=No trouble breathing, cough, or wheeze, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient specifically denied that the spinning is brought on by standing/standing up, contradicting the intake report.
Spinning episodes last only a few seconds, not longer.
Patient denied trouble breathing, cough, and wheeze individually; only 'breathing is perfectly fine' is recorded in ROS summary.
Meclizine was stopped because it made him too sleepy.
Ondansetron was prescribed by urgent care but was never taken/never started.
Ear exam details: both ear canals were clear, tympanic membranes looked normal, and there was no redness.
Right-sided Dix-Hallpike finding was a burst of torsional nystagmus lasting about 8 to 10 seconds and then fading/fatiguing.
